corpusSummary: Across 2026 papers on large language models, the corpus reveals a tension between ambitious AI capabilities and persistent gaps in embodiment, situated knowledge, and governance. Clusters include critical framings of LLM cognition and anthropomorphism; trust, ethics, and equity in health, education, and policy; AI-supported learning and concerns about dependency; and the emergence of LLMs as methodological tools requiring validation, transparency, and safety standards.

themes.name: Cognition, embodiment, and the limits of AI agency
themes.description: Maps cognition-like processes onto LLMs, highlights embodied knowledge gaps, and cautions against anthropomorphism and conflating AI outputs with subjective experience.

themes.name: Trust, governance, and responsible AI deployment
themes.description: Examines equity-focused governance, trust dynamics in AI counseling, and organizational and professional adoption barriers across sectors.

themes.name: AI in education and learning: pedagogy, literacy, and dependency
themes.description: Investigates AI tutoring, scaffolding, and learning analytics, plus risks of overreliance, ethical concerns, and the need for AI literacy.

themes.name: LLMs as research tools: opportunities, standards, and validation
themes.description: Explores LLM-enabled methods in policy, design, data analysis, and social science workflows, with emphasis on validation, transparency, and ethical oversight.

emergingKeywords: LLMs as research tools and standards
